name: Hodge structure

phase_0.boundary_condition: The terminal anchor of the algebraic variety's cohomology, where the Hodge filtration stabilizes and the global topological invariants are fixed.

⊢.justification: The void state before the Hodge filtration is applied; the raw vector space containing all cycles.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary where the filtration terminates and the algebraic structure is fully defined.

≻.justification: The forward morphism moving up the filtration levels, refining the subspace inclusion.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism descending via complex conjugation, establishing the dual subspace.

⋈.justification: The composition of boundary maps linking cohomology groups across different degrees.

⊙.justification: The self-referential identity where the subspace is defined by its own bidegree properties.

∈.justification: The co-multiplication splitting the cohomology into conjugate pairs of bidegree components.

∋.justification: The multiplication rejoining the conjugate arms to form the total cohomology class.

⊤.justification: The constructive proof that a specific bidegree component exists within the filtration.

⊥.justification: The constructive refutation that cycles outside the Hodge decomposition exist in the algebraic variety.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where the variety touches itself, holding both the algebraic and transcendental constraints simultaneously.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the integer invariants that remain stable under deformation.

phase_2.fuse_result: The unified cohomology class containing both bidegree components
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The raw cohomology group before any filtration or decomposition is applied.
phase_3.true_description: A cohomology class proven to lie within a specific Hodge filtration level F^p.
phase_3.false_description: A cycle refuted as not belonging to the algebraic Hodge decomposition.
phase_3.both_description: A critical point where the variety is both smooth and singular, or where algebraic and transcendental cycles coincide.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the raw cohomology group H^k(X, C) as the void state.
Apply the ascending Hodge filtration F^p to refine the subspace.
Split the cohomology into conjugate bidegree components H^{p,q} and H^{q,p}.
Affirm the existence of the H^{p,q} component on the T-arm.
Apply the conjugate filtration  ar{F}^q on the F-arm to establish the dual.
Refute any cycles that do not fit the H^{q,p} structure on the F-arm.
Compose the boundary maps to link the filtration levels in a long exact sequence.
Identify the self-referential nature of the H^{p,q} decomposition.
Engage the critical pinch point where the variety touches itself, holding both states.
Rejoin the T and F arms to reconstruct the total cohomology H^k.
Record the Hodge numbers h^{p,q} as permanent integer invariants.
Anchor the system at the stabilized filtration boundary.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Hodge filtration functor that translates topological cycles into algebraic subspaces.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The long exact sequence of cohomology groups linking different degrees.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The Hodge numbers h^{p,q} stored as immutable integer invariants.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The complex structure J that determines the order of filtration levels.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical Hodge decomposition theorem for compact Kähler manifolds.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational effort to resolve the bidegree decomposition.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The raw cohomology group with no filtration structure.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The fully decomposed Hodge structure with fixed invariants.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The Hodge numbers are topological invariants, so the decomposition preserves the total information content of the cohomology.

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑰: Hodge structures decompose cohomology into nested subspaces (Hodge filtration) that form a hierarchical, branched tree of inclusions.
⊢=𐑦: Hodge structures encode global topological information where boundary conditions and cohomology classes reflect the bulk properties, aligning with the scale-collapse primitive where surface and interior are unified.
⊞=𐑳: Hodge structures involve a decomposition into components of different types (p,q) with distinct counts, reflecting an asymmetric distribution rather than equal or higher-order symmetric pairing.
⊡=𐑭: Hodge structures are classified by discrete integer invariants (Hodge numbers) that remain stable under continuous deformations of the complex structure.
⊙=⊙: Hodge structures encode the critical cohomological data of algebraic varieties, reflecting scale-free correlations and maximal sensitivity characteristic of a system at a critical threshold.
⊥=𐑫: Hodge structures encode topological invariants that are robust against continuous deformations, implying a topological chirality that cannot be undone without global restructuring.
≻=𐑽: A Hodge structure decomposes cohomology into graded pieces via a filtration that stabilizes the underlying topological invariants without altering the fundamental cycle, acting adjointly to the complex structure.
≺=𐑬: A Hodge structure decomposes the cohomology into self-complementary subspaces $H^{p,q}$ and $H^{q,p}$, where the conjugation symmetry implies simultaneous donor and acceptor roles for the interface.
⋈=𐑐: Hodge structures impose rigid geometric constraints that ensure high-fidelity, deterministic interactions with near-certainty.
⊤=𐑧: Hodge structures represent rigid algebraic invariants that are kinetically frozen and require external driving (such as variation in complex structure) to rearrange.
∈=𐑔: Hodge structures encode global topological invariants where interactions propagate across the entire system via cohomology classes.
∋=𐑝: Hodge structures require the simultaneous presence of all weight-graded components to form a coherent algebraic system.
